tagline: The world's most isolated big city — 19 white beaches, quokkas on a car-free island, and sunsets over the Indian Ocean.
overview: Perth is famously the most isolated major city on earth — closer to Bali than Sydney — and it wears that remoteness as freedom: a laid-back capital of 19 white-sand beaches where the sun sets over the ocean (east-coast Australians never see that).

Kings Park, bigger than Central Park, tops the city with wildflower bushland and skyline views; Fremantle's harbour keeps its Victorian port streetscape and craft-beer scene; and Rottnest Island — car-free, 30 minutes by boat — is home to the quokka, the world's smiliest marsupial.
Speed's 2024 tour streamed from Perth. The state around it is a blockbuster — the Pinnacles desert, Margaret River's wineries and whale season are the signature day trips.
